project: PRD-251 Socials — Wave 3: schedule and publish
baseBranch: feat/prd-251-w2-socials-tab (stacked until Wave 2 is on main; then main)
description: Wave 3 of PRD-251 (docs/PRDS/PRD-251-SOCIALS.md — D1-D17 binding, plus the 'Waves 2+3 build' block at the top). The publisher and its five channel publishers (S3.3a-e: LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube; plus the generic adapter), scheduling with one-shot jobs, reconcile and missed slots (S3.1a), the calendar kind 'social' with drag to reschedule (S3.1b), the publish controls and receipts in the post view (S3.3f), and the end-to-end check of D14's one way out. Wave 2 built what publishing needs: media hosting (S3.4), the channel registry and adapter data (S3.2), channels as approved content (the hash covers the targets) and the post gate's PLATFORM_PUBLISHER way through (D14b). No migration: every status the wave uses already exists in core/models/socials.py (SOCIAL_POST_STATUSES, SOCIAL_TARGET_STATUSES). CI has no Composio connections: every channel is proven against a mocked executor; one live publish per channel is the owner's (docs/PRDS/prd251-w3-owner-test.md).

userStories.title: S3.3 — The publisher: a post's targets published through Composio, file-first, idempotent, with receipts
userStories.description: Fill the Wave 0 seam in orchestrator/modules/socials/publisher.py (publish_post, :1-38; PublishingUnavailable goes). ONE engine runs every channel; the channels differ only in the adapter DATA (modules/socials/channel_adapters.py, read through capabilities.py ChannelStep :343). Put the engine in new modules (e.g. modules/socials/publishing.py for the run, publish_sources.py for resolving step params) — service.py (992 lines) and api/socials.py (970 lines) are over 800: do not grow them beyond the few lines a transition or a route needs. The run: (1) assert_publishable (service.py:914) first, always; claim the post with a compare-and-set approved|scheduled → publishing (service.claim_unchanged) so two workers never both publish; (2) for each target not yet published (social_post_targets, targets.py; its action_plan holds the registry's resolved STEPS, targets.py:36,180), run its steps in order through ComposioToolExecutor.execute (core/composio/tool_executor.py:364) with way_through=PLATFORM_PUBLISHER (core/composio/post_gate.py:134) — the ONLY caller that passes it; the deny list still runs first and a denied step fails its target (or is skipped when optional). Resolve each step's params from their sources (channel_adapters.py docstring): $copy (the channel's own copy, else the base), $title, $media / $media[] (the post's rendered files, modules/socials/media_urls.py resolve_post_media :181), $media.content_type, $media.bytes, $thumbnail, $option.<name> (the target's options), $steps.<id> (a value an earlier step returned; define per step which result field it reads, in the adapter data), and a|b fallbacks. FILE-FIRST: a param named in the step's `files` is handed to the executor's file resolver (tool_executor.py:126 resolve_file_uploads) as the adapter's OWN upload spec — add a keyword (e.g. upload_params=) so the resolver converts exactly those params for this call; NEVER add a slug to the global UPLOAD_ACTIONS (:41). A param in `urls` takes a presigned inline link (media_urls presigned_inline_url, D9) and needs public storage: without SOCIALS_PUBLIC_MEDIA_BUCKET the step is skipped when optional, else the target fails saying so. A `status` step polls until done or SOCIALS_PUBLISH_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS (new config, e.g. 600) every SOCIALS_PUBLISH_POLL_SECONDS (new, e.g. 5). Retries (D8): a transient failure (timeout, 5xx, 429, a connection error) retries the target up to SOCIALS_MAX_TARGET_ATTEMPTS (config.py:1911, 3) with backoff SOCIALS_PUBLISH_RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS (new); a 4xx or a platform refusal does not retry and records the platform's message on the target (error). attempts counts every try. Receipts: on success the target stores remote_id and permalink (from the publish step's result: define the result fields per step in the adapter data), status published, published_at. The post ends published (all targets), partially_published (some) or failed (none), each logged in review_log; a failed or partially published post notifies (new event types social_post_failed, social_post_published in notification_dispatcher VALID_EVENT_TYPES :45; link_type social_post). Idempotency: a published target is never run again (its idempotency_key, targets.py:155, is passed to the platform where the action takes one); a retry runs only the failed targets. Routes: POST /api/socials/posts/{id}/publish-now (api/socials.py:727, CAN_UPDATE) now publishes — it answers 202 with the post in publishing and runs in the background (launch_guarded, as render does) — and POST /api/socials/posts/{id}/retry (new, CAN_UPDATE) re-runs the failed targets of a failed or partially_published post, only while its approval still matches (an assert_retryable beside assert_publishable). Status machine (service.py TRANSITIONS :116): publish {approved, scheduled, failed?, partially_published → publishing}, publish_done {publishing → published | partially_published | failed}; a post stuck in publishing is failed by the boot reaper like a stuck render (core/boot/reaper.py:217 _reap_social_renders is the precedent), leaving its published targets' receipts as they are. This story proves the engine with LinkedIn (S3.3a: text, image through the workspace-scoped image workaround core/composio/linkedin_image_workaround.py, video LINKEDIN_UPLOAD_VIDEO → LINKEDIN_CREATE_VIDEO_POST).
acceptanceCriteria: With a mocked ComposioToolExecutor: a LinkedIn text, image and video post each issue exactly the adapter's documented sequence, with way_through=PLATFORM_PUBLISHER, the files through the resolver's per-call upload spec, and store remote_id and permalink (tests). → DONE — CI run 36698181881 on d4d4651: orchestrator-tests green, running tests/test_prd251w3_publisher.py — test_a_linkedin_text_post_runs_the_adapter_sequence_and_stores_its_receipt, test_a_linkedin_image_post_hands_its_files_to_the_upload_spec and test_a_linkedin_video_uploads_then_posts_with_the_returned_video_urn assert each sequence, way_through=PLATFORM_PUBLISHER, the files as upload_params, and remote_id + permalink.

assert_publishable runs first: a stale approval publishes nothing and makes no executor call; two concurrent publishes of one post issue ONE sequence (compare-and-set claim; test on the CI Postgres). → DONE — CI run 36698181881 on d4d4651: test_a_stale_approval_claims_nothing_and_calls_nothing and test_a_run_whose_post_lost_its_approval_publishes_nothing (no executor call); test_two_concurrent_publishes_of_one_post_issue_one_sequence_on_postgres ran on the CI Postgres (its fixture raises rather than skips when CI is set) and passed: one claim, one LINKEDIN_CREATE_LINKED_IN_POST, also under a double run.

userStories.title: S3.3c — Instagram: image, Reel and carousel, container then publish
userStories.description: Run Instagram through the engine: INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA with image_file / video_file (file-first, the adapter's upload spec) → wait for the container (the publish action waits for processing; poll where the adapter has a status step) → INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH; carousel: one child container per image, then INSTAGRAM_CREATE_CAROUSEL_CONTAINER, then publish. Instagram needs JPEG images (Traps), and stills render as PNG today. Pillow is NOT an orchestrator dependency and a new dependency needs the owner's OK (AGENTS.md), so convert where the tools already are: ask media-render for a JPEG copy of the still (it has ffmpeg), or refuse the Instagram image target with a clear message; say which in the commit body. Never convert in the orchestrator with a new library. Never the deprecated actions (INSTAGRAM_CREATE_MEDIA_CONTAINER, INSTAGRAM_CREATE_POST, INSTAGRAM_GET_POST_STATUS). Never widen UPLOAD_ACTIONS.
acceptanceCriteria: With the executor mocked: an image, a Reel and a 3-slide carousel each issue the documented sequence, with the container id flowing into the publish step, and store the media id and permalink (tests). → DONE — CI run 36704196633 on 5ba7e6f: orchestrator-tests green, running tests/test_prd251w3_instagram.py — test_an_instagram_image_is_a_jpeg_container_waited_on_then_published, test_a_reel_uploads_its_video_file_unconverted and test_a_three_slide_carousel_sends_three_jpegs_to_one_carousel_container assert each sequence, the container id flowing into INSTAGRAM_POST_IG_USER_MEDIA_PUBLISH (), and the stored media id and permalink.

userStories.title: S3.1a — Scheduling: one-shot jobs, reconcile, and missed slots
userStories.description: D10. Scheduling a post (service.schedule :771 via POST /posts/{id}/schedule :696) registers an APScheduler DateTrigger job id social-publish-<post_id> on the unified scheduler (services/scheduler.py; one leader holds the fcntl lock, main.py:419), registered with a module-level function and plain args (post_id, workspace_id as strings), never a closure, so the RedisJobStore can pickle it (precedent: services/scheduled_task_service.py:706). Unschedule (:712), an edit that voids approval, reject/archive and a reschedule (POST /schedule on a scheduled post: the slot moves, the approval stands — add the scheduled→scheduled move to TRANSITIONS) remove or move the job. A request usually lands on a worker without the scheduler: add a socials pass to services/schedule_reconcile.py run_reconcile_once (:34) that registers a job for every scheduled post, removes jobs whose post is no longer scheduled, and runs every RECONCILE_INTERVAL_SECONDS (scheduled_task_service.py:41). The job runs the US-301 publisher (its claim makes a double fire publish once). Missed slot: when the job fires (or the reconcile finds a scheduled post whose slot passed) later than SOCIALS_MISFIRE_GRACE_SECONDS (config.py:1909) after the slot, the post goes to missed (service transition scheduled → missed) and the owner is notified (event social_post_missed); within the grace it publishes. A missed post can be rescheduled or published now while its approval still matches (stale content is never posted silently).
acceptanceCriteria: Scheduling registers social-publish-<post_id> with picklable args; unschedule, a voiding edit and reject remove it; a reschedule moves it and keeps the approval (tests with a fake scheduler).
The reconcile pass registers a missing job and removes an orphan; a job firing twice publishes once (tests; the double fire on the CI Postgres).
A slot missed by more than the grace ends missed with a notification and publishes nothing; within the grace it publishes; a missed post can be rescheduled (tests).

userStories.title: S3.1b — The calendar: social posts in the Command Center calendar, drag to reschedule
userStories.description: D10 Calendar. Backend: a sixth source _social_post_items beside the five in services/activity_service.py (:906-912) — the file is 1,327 lines, so the source lives in a NEW module (e.g. services/activity_social_items.py) and activity_service only adds it to the tuple. Each scheduled post in the window becomes an item: id social-<post_id>, type 'social', name the post title, next_run_at its slot (UTC ISO), plus post_id and timezone (social_posts.timezone) so the UI shows the time in the post's own timezone; only while Socials is on for the workspace (settings.socials_state); scoped to the caller's workspace. Frontend: the kind 'social' in the three union files — ScheduleItemType (frontend/hooks/use-activity-api.ts:97), components/command-center/calendar-kinds.ts, components/command-center/calendar-actions.ts (a case 'social'). Clicking an item opens /deliverables?tab=socials&post=<id>. A Reschedule menu item and drag-and-drop (native HTML5 drag events, NO new npm dependency) call POST /api/socials/posts/{id}/schedule with the new slot and the post's timezone: the slot moves, the approval stands. calendar-tab.tsx is 1,019 lines: put the drag and the social item's rendering in new files and add only the hooks it needs.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend: a scheduled post appears as social-<post_id> with its slot and timezone; another workspace's post and a post that is not scheduled never appear; with Socials off there are no social items (tests).
vitest: the social kind renders with its label and colour, shows the time in the post's timezone, opens the post on click, and Reschedule and a drop call the schedule route with the new slot.
No new npm dependency; the three union files carry 'social' (gate).

userStories.title: S3.3f — Publish controls and receipts in the post view
userStories.description: Extend the post view (frontend/components/deliverables/socials/socials-post-detail.tsx and the US-206 split files; keep each component ≤150 lines, add new files): for an approved post, Schedule (a date-time picker; the timezone from the browser, Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone, sent to POST /schedule) and Publish now (a confirmation naming the channels); for a scheduled post, its slot in the post's timezone, Reschedule and Unschedule; for a publishing post, per-target progress while it polls (reuse the list's poll, use-socials-api.ts renderPollInterval pattern); for a published / partially_published / failed post, each target's receipt — status, permalink (opens the live post), the platform's error — and Retry for the failed targets (POST /retry, US-301); for a missed post, 'Missed its slot' with Reschedule and Publish now.
